sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Partial Differential Equations: From Classical to Modern (2025 archived author manuscript, AMS Graduate Studies in Mathematics)
sources.locator: Chapter 7, §7.1 (printed pp. 166-172), §7.2 (printed pp. 172-176) and §7.3 (printed pp. 176-178), read in full for the named results and exercises listed below; the PDF was fetched at harvest time (source-fetch-check --stamp) and the printed page numbers are the text's own.

contents.name: §7.1, Kirchhoff's formula (7.10) and Theorem 7.2 (C^3 displacement, C^2 velocity data)
contents.support: The published item states this formula and theorem with the same conventions; its locator (§7.1, printed pp. 168-169) matches the text read here, including the C^2(R^4) conclusion.

contents.name: §7.1, Corollary 7.3 (Duhamel principle (7.11)-(7.13) for a C^{0;2} source)
contents.support: The theorem's source-term step is exactly Teschl's proof: integrate U(s,t,x)=(t-s)/(4pi) int_{S^2} f(s,x+(t-s)w) dw in s and differentiate with the Leibniz rule, using U_tt=Delta U and U_t(s,s,x)=f(s,x); the smooth h of the statement satisfies Teschl's C^{0;2} hypothesis, and no spatial compact support is required.

contents.name: §7.1, retarded potential (7.13)
contents.reason: The retarded-potential convolution and its distributional kernel belong to the later causal-kernel pair, where lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel records them; this pair claims only the smooth Cauchy representation.

contents.name: §7.1-§7.2, Huygens-principle remark (two- versus three-dimensional dependence on the data)
contents.reason: This is a qualitative comparison of the 2D and 3D formulas; the underlying descent formula is already published as thm-poisson-formula-for-the-two-dimensional-wave-equation and no claim of this pair rests on the remark.

contents.name: §7.2, spherical means (7.16) and the Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation (7.17)
contents.support: The published item states the same identity Delta_x M = M_rr + (n-1)/r M_r for spherical means of C^2 data with the continuity extension at r=0; read and matched.

contents.name: §7.2, Lemma 7.6 and the radial recursion (7.18)-(7.19)
contents.support: The published recursion lemma covers the D_r-transformation identity that reduces the Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation to the one-dimensional wave equation in odd dimensions.

contents.name: §7.2, Theorem 7.7 (odd-dimensional formula (7.23))
contents.support: The published odd-dimensional formula by iterated spherical means restates this theorem for h in C^{k+1} and g in C^{k+2} with n=2k+1.

contents.name: §7.2, Theorem 7.8 (even-dimensional formula (7.24))
contents.support: The published even-dimensional formula by descent restates this theorem for n=2k.

contents.name: §7.2, Corollary 7.9 (Duhamel in general dimensions (7.25)-(7.26))
contents.support: The proof of the general-dimension Duhamel corollary follows the same two-step pattern (launch the source as velocity data, integrate and differentiate); the three-dimensional case with the general smooth source of this pair is what the item's source-term step records, and the n>=2 generality is not restated here.

contents.name: §7.1-§7.2, Problem* 7.10 (spherical means satisfy the Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation)
contents.support: The exercise is carried out by the published Euler-Poisson-Darboux item, which proves the identity rather than assuming it.

contents.name: §7.1-§7.2, Problems 7.1-7.9 and 7.11-7.14 (Stokes' rule, radial reductions, Klein-Gordon variants, worked examples)
contents.reason: These exercises ask the reader to derive examples and variants (Stokes' rule, radial solutions, Klein-Gordon analogues, Fourier-transform identities) that no item of this pair claims; the mathematics of this pair's scope is fully covered by the results listed above.

contents.name: §7.3, Lemma 7.10 and Theorem 7.11 (bounded-domain energy conservation and Dirichlet uniqueness)
contents.support: The published bounded-domain energy uniqueness theorem states the same conservation identity and its uniqueness corollary for the Dirichlet problem with the outward-normal convention.

contents.name: §7.3, Theorem 7.12 (cone of dependence via the local energy on the shrinking ball)
contents.support: The published finite-propagation theorem formalises exactly this computation: if u and u_t vanish on the base ball then u vanishes on the closed backward cone; the proof read here is the local-energy argument quoted.

contents.name: §7.3, Corollary 7.13 (uniqueness on R^n for C^2 solutions with continuous data)
contents.support: The published local-uniqueness theorem is the two-solution form of this corollary on a backward cone and is the supplier used for clauses (b) and (c); included is the fact that no finite-energy hypothesis is needed.

contents.name: §7.3, Problem 7.15 (energy computation for Lemma 7.10)
contents.reason: The exercise re-derives the bounded-domain energy identity that is already published as thm-energy-uniqueness-for-homogeneous-dirichlet-waves-on-bounded-domains, and this pair makes no use of the bounded-domain result.

sources.title: Victor Ivrii, Partial Differential Equations (University of Toronto, 2018, CC BY-SA)
sources.locator: Chapter 9, §9.1.1-§9.1.4 (printed pp. 281-288) and §9.2.1-§9.2.3 (printed pp. 288-292), read in full for the named results listed below; the PDF was fetched at harvest time (source-fetch-check --stamp).

contents.name: §9.1.1-§9.1.2, Kirchhoff formulas (9.1.4), (9.1.8)-(9.1.10) for the 3D Cauchy problem
contents.support: The published Kirchhoff formula and the attain-the-data lemma restate (9.1.10) in the same c-parametrisation; (9.1.8) is identified as t*M_{c|t|}h.

contents.name: §9.1.2, Duhamel integral (9.1.11) and Kirchhoff formula with source (9.1.12)
contents.support: Writing s=t-tau, Ivrii's source term is int_0^t (1/(4 pi c^2 s)) int_{S(x,cs)} f(y,tau) dsigma dtau = int_0^t (t-tau) M_{c(t-tau)} f(.,tau)(x) dtau; with the right-hand side f=c^2 h of W u = h this is exactly the c^2 int H_{h(.,v)} dv source term of the theorem.

contents.name: §9.1.2, retarded potential (a.k.a. time-delayed potential) (9.1.13)
contents.reason: The retarded-potential representation is the topic of the later causal-kernel pair (lem-em-retarded-wave-kernel and its consumers); it is recorded here only as a destination, not built on this page.

contents.name: §9.1.3, Definition 9.1.1 of the spherical mean (9.1.14)
contents.support: The published definition of the spherical mean and the weighted ball integral matches (9.1.14), including the surface-area normalisation omega_2=4pi.

contents.name: §9.1.3, Remark 9.1.3 (spherical-mean proof of Kirchhoff; rM_r solves the one-dimensional wave equation)
contents.support: The published ball-and-sphere mean radial identity states the relation used to view v=rM_r as a one-dimensional wave solution; the Euler-Poisson-Darboux relation itself is the published item cited above.

contents.name: §9.1.4, 2D wave equation by the method of descent
contents.support: The published Poisson formula is the descent result derived in this subsection; this pair does not restate the two-dimensional formula.

contents.name: §9.2.1, local energy identity (9.2.1)-(9.2.3)
contents.support: The published local energy identity is (9.2.2) with the same sign convention q=-c^2 u_t Du; read and matched.

contents.name: §9.2.2, Proposition 9.2.1 and Definition 9.2.1 (positivity of the boundary form; space-like, characteristic and time-like surfaces)
contents.support: The positivity and classification statements are precisely the pointwise input used in the published local-uniqueness theorem's truncated-cone energy argument, which is the supplier of the theorem's clauses (b) and (c).

contents.name: §9.2.3, Theorems 9.2.2 and 9.2.3 (vanishing on a cone and local uniqueness)
contents.support: The published local-uniqueness theorem is the formal version of Theorem 9.2.3, with the closed backward cone and the base-ball data condition; the proof was read in full here.

contents.name: §9.2.4, Theorem 9.2.4 (initial-boundary value problem on a spatial domain)
contents.reason: Boundary-value problems on spatial domains lie outside this pair's whole-space scope; the theorem of this page explicitly asserts nothing about finite-domain boundary conditions.

canonical.name: Joint C^infty smoothness in (x,s,v) of the spherical-mean family M(x,s,v)=(4pi)^{-1} int_{S^2} h(x+sn,v) dOmega, with every differentiated-integral formula
canonical.support: Not a named textbook theorem: it is the parameter-differentiation step used silently in both sources (Teschl §7.1, printed pp. 167-170, and Ivrii §9.1.3, printed pp. 284-285) when the means are differentiated in x, t and the source parameter; localised here as an explicit prerequisite for the source term of the theorem.

canonical.name: The c^2-normalised source term c^2 int_{t_0}^t H_{h(.,v)}(x,t-v) dv and its verification by the moving-endpoint Leibniz rule (the W2 computation)
canonical.support: The computation is the two-source Duhamel derivation specialised to the operator W=c^{-2} partial_t^2 - Delta with right-hand side h; the c^2 factor converts the right-hand side h of W u = h into the source c^2 h of Box_c u = c^2 h.
